title: rpi_ctrl_v2.sh: channel readback overwritten, indigo3 versions installed as indigo, open networks rejected
description:
Small fixes in tools/rpi_ctrl_v2.sh (VERSION 2.01), item A of upstream issue #787. The password-length guards are handled by the related ticket ea48a942.

1. __read-wifi-channel tests WIFI_AP_CH instead of the local wifi_ch it just read, so WIFI_AP_CH (default 6) is always overwritten with the read value, which is empty when no indigo-wifi profile is active (for example a Raspberry Pi Imager install connected through netplan-wlan0-<SSID>). --get-wifi-channel then alerts "'channel' not found" in client mode instead of exiting quietly, and --set-wifi-server falls back to auto channel selection. Expected: keep the current value when the read is empty.
2. __install-version always runs apt-get install indigo=<version>, but __list-available-versions also lists indigo3 versions, which then fail to install. Expected: install the package (indigo or indigo3) that owns the version, e.g. by checking apt-cache show indigo3=<version>.
3. __set-wifi-client rejects an empty password (WIFI_CN_PW not set), so open networks cannot be joined although indigo_server passes '' for an empty password. Expected: an empty password joins an open network (nmcli dev wifi connect <ssid> without password); a non-empty password keeps the 8..63 length check.
4. The argument parser prints 'unknown argument ${2}' instead of the unknown argument ${1}.

No change to the CLI or to the OK / ALERT output format. Tests: a hardware-free test that runs the script with stub nmcli, apt-get, apt-cache, iw, raspi-config on PATH and checks the commands issued and the output for each case. Observed on Raspberry Pi OS trixie with indigo3 3.0-11.

outcome.summary: Pass. Diff vs ticket/ea48a942 reviewed (tools/rpi_ctrl_v2.sh, test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py, Makefile, AGENTS.md, pbxproj). (1) rpi_ctrl_v2.sh:317 assigns the read channel only when non-empty; client mode without indigo-wifi now exits 1 quietly, active AP readback unchanged. (2) :553-555 output-based apt-cache show indigo3=<ver> check is right: host apt 2.8.4 prints nothing and exits 0 for a missing version (exits 100 only for an unknown package), stderr discarded, so the check is robust to either. (3) :449-462 guards run only for non-empty passwords and still __ALERT before any nmcli call; indigo_server's '' reaches the parser as an empty $2; open connect is quoted; failed open connect keeps the AP fallback. (4) :667 prints ${1}. Tests: make test-rpi-ctrl-v2 8/8 OK and test-rpi-ctrl-wifi-client 3/3 OK on this tree; read against the parent script each of the four defect tests fails (ALERT 'channel' not found, indigo=3.0-11 argv, WIFI_CN_PW not set, empty ${2}). Safety: PATH is stubs + grep/head/tr/which only, CONF_SYSCTL/PROC_FORWARD redirected and /etc|/proc absence asserted, /sys carrier read goes through the cat stub and is unreachable in these cases. Portability: PCRE case skips without grep -P; the other cases do not depend on GNU tools; /bin/bash 3.2 compatible. Xcode ID unique, git diff --check clean. Out of scope, for the owner (not required here): after a successful open join, update_wifi_setings (indigo_server.c:1543) runs --get-wifi-client and --get-wifi-server, which __ALERT "'psk' not found" (rpi_ctrl_v2.sh:477, :375) because an open profile has no psk [verify on hardware], so SERVER_WIFI_INFRASTRUCTURE (and AP) end in ALERT with a blank SSID although the join succeeded. Fixing it changes the get-commands' ALERT behaviour, which this ticket excluded; suggest a follow-up ticket.

Round 2 pass at tree 0cdad9c3 (commit 51b2c3b94). Delta: rpi_ctrl_v2.sh:376 (__get-wifi-server) and :491 (__get-wifi-client) alert "'psk' not found" only when psk is empty and the active profile has 802-11-wireless-security.key-mgmt; [[ && ]] short-circuits, so the extra nmcli call happens only when psk is empty; the lookbehind key regex cannot match another key. indigo_server consumption (indigo_server.c:986-1031, called after --set-wifi-client at :1543, non-verbose): open client profile -> --get-wifi-client prints the SSID, so SERVER_WIFI_INFRASTRUCTURE is OK with the SSID and a cleared password; --get-wifi-server in client mode exits 1 with no output, so execute_query returns NULL and SERVER_WIFI_AP goes IDLE, as for a secured client; the attach-time 30 s retry (:1172) no longer fires for open networks. Verbose 'SSID<TAB>' gives an SSID token and no password token. Secured profiles without psk (wpa-psk, and wpa-eap/WEP/OWE, which also have key-mgmt) still alert as before. Tests: test_get_wifi_settings_of_open_network fails on the round-1 script (all four subtests print the ALERT) and passes now; the secured-without-psk test guards against over-relaxing; require_pcre is a straight extraction. make test-rpi-ctrl-v2 10/10 OK, 0 skipped; make test-rpi-ctrl-wifi-client 3/3 OK; git diff --check clean; AGENTS.md entry accurate. Coverage limit: open-profile nmcli output verified on a laptop NetworkManager, not on the Pi's [verify].

history.text: Writing indigo_test/unit/test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py to reproduce the four defects
Running test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py on the unfixed script (reproduction)

Reproduction (before fix) with indigo_test/unit/test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py on the unmodified tools/rpi_ctrl_v2.sh (stub-only PATH, CONF_SYSCTL/PROC_FORWARD redirected): 8 tests, 4 failures, one per defect. (1) --get-wifi-channel, no indigo-wifi profile active (nmcli exits 10, no output): stdout "ALERT: 'channel' not found" instead of a quiet exit 1. (2) --install-version 3.0-11 with apt-cache show indigo3=3.0-11 returning a record: apt-get argv was 'install -y --allow-downgrades indigo=3.0-11', expected indigo3=3.0-11. (3) --set-wifi-client fixture-net '': stdout 'ALERT: WIFI_CN_PW not set', expected OK and 'nmcli dev wifi connect fixture-net' with no password. (4) --bogus-option: printed 'unknown argument ' (empty ${2}). Passing before the fix: active AP channel readback (11), indigo (2.x) version install, 1/7/64-char password rejection without commands (the __ALERT guards from ea48a942 are already on this branch's base), 8/63-char join. Host check: apt 2.8.4 'apt-cache show bash=<missing version>' prints nothing and exits 0 (only an unknown package exits 100), so the indigo3 test must use the output, not the exit status.
Fixing the four defects in tools/rpi_ctrl_v2.sh
Running test-rpi-ctrl-v2 and test-rpi-ctrl-wifi-client after the fix
Check command-1 started: make -C indigo_test test-rpi-ctrl-v2

After fix: test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py 8/8 pass, none skipped (flow check --command 'make -C indigo_test test-rpi-ctrl-v2' passed; whitespace passed). test_rpi_ctrl_wifi_client.py from ea48a942 also still passes 3/3. Changes in tools/rpi_ctrl_v2.sh: (1) __read-wifi-channel assigns the read wifi_ch only when it is non-empty, otherwise WIFI_AP_CH keeps its value (default 6); (2) __install-version installs indigo3=<ver> when 'apt-cache show indigo3=<ver>' prints a record, otherwise indigo=<ver>. It checks the output rather than the exit status because apt 2.8 exits 0 with no output for a missing version. Behaviour of trixie's apt 3.x not checked [verify]; the output check works either way. (3) __set-wifi-client: an empty password runs 'nmcli dev wifi connect <ssid>' without password; the 8..63 length guards apply only to a non-empty password. (4) the parser prints 'unknown argument ${1}'. Coordination with ea48a942: this ticket's branch is based on ea48a942's branch (HEAD includes its two wip commits), so the __ALERT length guards are already in the base. Fix (3) moves both guards into the non-empty branch and keeps __ALERT, so a 1..7 or >63-char password still alerts before any nmcli call (tested with 1, 7 and 64 chars, no command issued). Open-network failure keeps the existing fallback: checked by hand with a failing connect stub, the script prints 'ALERT: failed to connect ... WiFi set to default AP' and rebuilds the indigosky AP. Not changed: VERSION=2.01, tools/rpi_ctrl.sh. Limitations: unit check not run because libusb-1.0/avahi-client dev packages are missing on this host; the active-AP channel case skips on hosts whose grep lacks -P (e.g. macOS BSD grep); the script itself needs GNU grep -P. Makefile.inc (gitignored) was generated in the worktree with 'make Makefile.inc' because indigo_test/Makefile includes it.
Reviewing rpi_ctrl_v2.sh diff vs parent branch
Checking host apt-cache show output for missing versions/packages

Coordinator addition after review round 1 (pass): open-network support must also read back cleanly. After an open join, indigo_server re-reads (indigo_server.c ~1543); --get-wifi-client (rpi_ctrl_v2.sh ~477) and --get-wifi-server (~375) alert 'psk' not found because an open profile has no psk, so the properties go to ALERT although the join worked. Fix in this ticket: treat a missing psk as an open network when the profile has no 802-11-wireless-security.key-mgmt (empty password, no alert); keep alerting for a secured profile without psk. Output format unchanged otherwise.
Coordinator addition: open-profile psk readback in --get-wifi-client/--get-wifi-server

Coordinator addition (open-profile settings readback), reproduction before the fix: added test_get_wifi_settings_of_open_network and test_get_wifi_settings_of_secured_network_without_psk to test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py (stub nmcli -s con show: active indigo-wifi client profile with ssid/mode only, and one with key-mgmt wpa-psk but no psk). On the unfixed script --get-wifi-client, --verbose --get-wifi-client, --get-wifi-server and --verbose --get-wifi-server all printed "ALERT: 'psk' not found" for the open profile (4 subtest failures). indigo_server update_wifi_setings (indigo_server.c ~986-1030) reads only the first line via execute_query: an 'ALERT:' prefix sets SERVER_WIFI_AP / SERVER_WIFI_INFRASTRUCTURE to ALERT and clears the SSID, so after an open join the infrastructure property showed ALERT with a blank SSID. The secured-without-psk case already alerted, as expected.
Running flow checks after the open-profile readback fix
Check command-1 started: make -C indigo_test test-rpi-ctrl-v2
Check command-1 started: make -C indigo_test test-rpi-ctrl-wifi-client

Coordinator addition, after the fix: --get-wifi-client and --get-wifi-server now alert "'psk' not found" only when the psk is empty AND the active profile has 802-11-wireless-security.key-mgmt. With no key-mgmt (open network) the password is empty. Open client profile: --get-wifi-client prints 'open-net' (exit 0), so indigo_server sets SERVER_WIFI_INFRASTRUCTURE OK with the SSID. --verbose prints 'open-net<TAB>' for both commands; strtok_r gives the SSID and no password token, so the password is cleared. --get-wifi-server in client mode exits 1 with no output, so execute_query returns NULL and SERVER_WIFI_AP goes IDLE, the same as for a secured client profile. A secured profile without psk still alerts for both commands. flow check on tree 0cdad9c3: test-rpi-ctrl-v2 10/10 passed, 0 skipped; test-rpi-ctrl-wifi-client 3/3 passed; whitespace passed. Unverified on real NetworkManager: that 'nmcli -s con show' prints no 802-11-wireless-security lines for an open profile [verify]. If it printed 'key-mgmt: --' the open case would still alert. indigo_test/AGENTS.md entry updated.

Verified on real NetworkManager (Ubuntu laptop, read-only): for two saved open Wi-Fi profiles, 'nmcli con show <name>' prints no 802-11-wireless-security lines at all and 'nmcli -g 802-11-wireless-security.key-mgmt' is empty, matching the open-network stub used in test_rpi_ctrl_v2.py. Not yet checked on the Pi's NetworkManager version.
